items.title: fix: support CRLF configuration and current Links Notation consumers
items.body:
## Summary

Windows CRLF `.lenv` files retained `\r` in JavaScript configuration values, breaking exact market, boolean and flavour comparisons. Recognize CRLF delimiters without trimming meaningful whitespace. LF, CRLF and mixed files now produce equivalent values, including duplicate keys, quoted values and multiline blocks. Literal carriage returns are preserved outside CRLF delimiters; the writer continues using LF.

Update `links-notation` from `^0.11.2` to `>=0.25.2 <0.28.0`, locked to **0.27.1**, the latest release assessed on 2026-10-29. Packed consumer tests verify one shared parser installation alongside **0.25.2, 0.26.0 and 0.27.1**, without overrides or a separate dedupe command. A latest-only caret range would still install a second copy for the reported 0.25.2 consumer.

The current dependency exports `Parser` and `Link`; tests exercise parsing, formatting, equality and construction. Lino-env already uses its own `: ` reader, so there are no upstream parser calls to migrate. The compatibility assessment preserves existing `.lenv` whitespace and quote semantics. Releases starting at 0.28 require another assessment.

Rust already recognizes CRLF through `str::lines()`. Add integration tests confirming the same configuration and roundtrip behavior, document it, and update an existing assertion for current Clippy. JavaScript's patch changeset and Rust's changelog fragment prepare the automatic releases.

## Reproduction and regression coverage

```js
writeFileSync(path, 'LAZADA_MARKET: vn\r\nSPACE:   preserve  \r\n');
new LinoEnv(path).read().toObject();
// Before: { LAZADA_MARKET: 'vn\r', SPACE: '  preserve  \r' }
// After:  { LAZADA_MARKET: 'vn',   SPACE: '  preserve  ' }
```

- `js/tests/line-endings.test.mjs`: 10 cases; **6 failed before the fix**, all pass afterward. Covers LF/CRLF with and without final newlines, mixed endings, spaces/tabs, embedded and final literal CR, empty values, colons, duplicate keys, single/double quotes, multiline blocks, read/write/read and environment injection. Consumer choices include Nha Trang, `vn`, true/false, sorting and chocolate/unflavoured.
- `js/tests/links-notation.test.mjs`: public parser API and parse/format/parse tests for LF and CRLF.
- `js/experiments/verify-consumer-install.mjs`: installs the packed library into three temporary real consumers, verifies the lockfile and module resolution share one parser, and checks configuration and parser roundtrips at each version.
- `rust/tests/line_endings.rs`: two integration tests covering the equivalent preferences, duplicate keys, spaces, quotes, multiline blocks, literal CR and read/write/read.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm test`: 35 tests pass.
- [x] `bun test`: 35 tests pass.
- [x] `deno test --allow-read --allow-write --allow-env`: 35 tests pass.
- [x] `npm run test:consumer`: all three parser versions deduplicate and pass roundtrips with npm 11 and npm 10.8.2 (`npm exec --yes --package=npm@10.8.2 -- npm run test:consumer`).
- [x] `npm run check`: ESLint, Prettier and file size checks pass.
- [x] `node scripts/validate-changeset.mjs`: the single patch changeset is valid.
- [x] `cargo test --all-features -j 1`: 20 unit tests, 2 integration tests and 12 doctests pass.
- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo build --release -j 1` and `cargo package --list` pass.

CI runs configuration and parser tests across Node.js, Bun and Deno on Linux, macOS and Windows, plus the packed consumer checks on each OS with Node.js. Deno uses npm's locked installation and manual node_modules mode because its automatic bare-import resolver rejects this compound dependency range; Node types retain type checking. Test jobs have a ten-minute bound. Rust tests run on all three operating systems.

CI passed on final commit `c43d92a`: [JavaScript (nine runtime/OS combinations and consumer checks)](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-env/actions/runs/40963477691), [Rust (three OS, lint and package build)](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-env/actions/runs/40963477594). Both runs started on 2026-10-29 at 22:08:08 UTC, after that commit.

Fixes #35
Fixes #32
Fixes #33

items.title: Assess and update the Links Notation range for latest consumer interoperability
items.body: Installed lino-env 0.2.8 declares links-notation ^0.11.2, while the consumer root uses current links-notation 0.25.2. The npm graph keeps a nested 0.11.2 copy and prevents an all-latest own-maintained grammar graph without a potentially unsafe override. Please assess the current parser API, migrate the range with roundtrip and cross-platform configuration tests, and document compatibility. This is a maintenance/deduplication request, not a claim that the old version caused a local app failure. Keep current behavior verified, including existing CRLF regression issue #32. A coordinated lino-arguments dependency migration is requested separately; browser-commander#168 reports its analogous older range. Consumer validation reference: https://github.com/konard/vietnam-accomodation-search/commit/20ac35d50129157769c2460d88ffe564ceab7d73 . No private inputs are involved.

items.title: fix: prefer crates.io trusted publishing with token fallback
items.body:
Prefer crates.io trusted publishing for both automatic and manual instant Rust releases, with the existing token secrets retained as fallbacks.

- Grant `id-token: write` only to the publishing jobs and use `rust-lang/crates-io-auth-action`, pinned to v1.0.5's commit. Remove the inline `cargo publish --token` argument and the workflow-wide token environment variable.
- Try OIDC authentication first with `continue-on-error: true`. Pass `${{ steps.prm_auth.outputs.token || secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN || secrets.CARGO_TOKEN }}` through the publishing step's `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` environment variable. Keep both secrets available.
- Read `${PIPESTATUS[0]}` after piping Cargo output through `tee`. Previously, authentication and network failures returned success because `$?` captured `tee`'s exit code. Existing crate versions still succeed without publishing again.
- Merge current `main`, including its existing Clippy assertion fix and all CRLF/parser compatibility changes.
- Move JavaScript and Rust release tooling to Node.js 24. Current `command-stream`/Execa dependencies require Node.js 22 or newer and fail during import on Node.js 20. Keep the library's Node.js 20/Bun/Deno test matrix. PR checks now import the actual release dependencies and execute a harmless command before a release can change versions or publish.
- Document publisher registration and fallback priority. Update the Rust patch fragment and the existing JavaScript patch changeset; this repository permits exactly one JavaScript changeset at a time.

Reproduction and investigation:

- Original PR run [38428842228](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-env/actions/runs/38428842228) ran on `8829134` immediately after the October 13 commit. Downloaded log lines 681–697 identify `clippy::assert_is_empty` at `rust/src/lib.rs:713`; the earlier run [38417772870](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-env/actions/runs/38417772870) has the same failure. Local Clippy reproduced it before merging main's fix.
- Default-branch [Rust run 40964289766](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-env/actions/runs/40964289766) (downloaded log lines 3079–3093) and [JavaScript run 40964289714](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-env/actions/runs/40964289714) (lines 3264–3278) fail with `TypeError: TEXT_ENCODINGS.union is not a function` under Node.js 20.20.2. `npm exec --yes --package=node@20 -- node experiments/verify-release-runtime.mjs` reproduces the error; the same probe passes on Node.js 24.22.2.
- `node experiments/test-crates-publishing.mjs` executes the actual shell blocks from both release jobs using fake Cargo and fake credentials. Six of fourteen cases failed before the exit-status fix; all fourteen pass afterward. It covers upload success, both existing-version messages, invalid/missing credentials, network failures, OIDC permissions, action pinning, matching release conditions and fallback configuration. It never uploads a crate.

Validation completed locally:

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` with warnings denied, and Rust file-size checks.
- `cargo test --all-features -j 1`: 20 unit tests, 2 integration tests and 12 doctests.
- `cargo build --release -j 1` and `cargo package --allow-dirty`, including archive compilation/verification.
- `npm test`, `bun test`, and `deno test --allow-read --allow-write --allow-env`: 35 tests each.
- `npm run test:consumer`: packed consumers share one Links Notation installation at 0.25.2, 0.26.0 and 0.27.1.
- `npm run check`, changeset validation, and Actionlint 1.7.12 syntax/expression validation (ShellCheck unavailable locally).
- Fourteen publishing regression checks and the real release-tool import probe on Node.js 24.

After merge, `package-registry-manager setup --registry crates-io --migrate --execute` registers the trusted publisher on crates.io using a crate owner's authenticated session. The publisher must identify `link-foundation/lino-env` and the top-level workflow filename `rust.yml`, with no GitHub environment. Keep both token secrets as fallbacks before and after registration. Live OIDC publishing is exercised by a release after registration; PR validation uses mocks and does not publish packages.

Final CI passed on commit `62d5567b0d44c3f0ccbd9665b1d76c1919dfdf86`: [Rust](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-env/actions/runs/40969839356) (three OS test jobs, lint, package build and release workflow checks) and [JavaScript](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-env/actions/runs/40969839355) (all nine runtime/OS combinations, consumer installation checks and lint). Both runs started on 2026-10-29 at 22:58:37 UTC, six seconds after the commit. There are no failed or pending checks.

items.title: Support multi-line quoted strings with " and ' delimiters
We should drop support for multiple values of the same variable name
items.body:
At the moment we have support of multiple values of the same variable like this:

```
A: value1
A: value2
```

That should be dropped, in favor of rewrite. Meaning after such file is read and interpreted `A` = `value2`.

If we really need to support multiple values (array-like, link references sequence), we can do like this:

```
A: value1 value2
```

or

```
A: (value1 value2)
```

or

```
A: 
  value1
  value2
```

or

or

```
A: (
  value1
  value2
)
```

All valid links notation for `['value1', 'value2']`.

It should be done in both JavaScript and Rust versions, and note that this is breaking change for lino-env packages.

Both code and docs should be updated.

items.title: feat: add crates.io publishing support to Rust CI/CD workflow
items.body:
## Summary

This PR adds crates.io publishing support to the Rust CI/CD workflow, following the pattern from the [links-notation](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation) repository.

### Changes

- **Workflow updates** (`.github/workflows/rust.yml`):
  - Added `CARGO_TOKEN` secret environment variable for crates.io authentication
  - Added "Publish to Crates.io" step to both `auto-release` and `manual-release` jobs
  - Handles "already exists" case gracefully to avoid failing when version already published
  - Publishes to crates.io before creating GitHub release

- **Release script updates** (`rust/scripts/create-github-release.mjs`):
  - Added `--tag-prefix` option to support different tag formats (e.g., "rust-v")
  - Added `--crates-io-url` option to include crates.io link in release notes
  - GitHub releases now include a link to the crates.io package

- **Documentation updates** (`README.md`):
  - Updated Rust package status from "Coming soon" to crates.io badge
  - Added CI/CD Configuration section documenting both JavaScript and Rust publishing approaches:
    - **JavaScript**: Uses [NPM trusted publishing](https://docs.npmjs.com/trusted-publishers) with OIDC - configured on npmjs.com as a trusted publisher, requires `id-token: write` permission in workflow, no manual token needed
    - **Rust**: Requires `CARGO_TOKEN` secret for crates.io publishing
  - Clarified the differences between NPM trusted publishing (automatic, OIDC-based) and Rust publishing (requires manual token configuration)

### Setup Required

Repository maintainers need to add the `CARGO_TOKEN` secret to GitHub:

1. Go to [crates.io API tokens](https://crates.io/settings/tokens)
2. Create a new token with publish permissions for `lino-env`
3. Add it as a repository secret named `CARGO_TOKEN`

Note: No setup is needed for JavaScript publishing - it uses NPM trusted publishing which is already configured.

## Test Plan

- [x] YAML workflow syntax validated
- [x] Rust tests pass (20 unit tests + 14 doc tests)
- [x] Clippy lints pass
- [x] `cargo publish --dry-run` succeeds
- [x] CI workflow runs successfully on this PR

Fixes #22

items.title: Make a proof of concept
items.body:
Based on https://github.com/deep-assistant/hive-mind/blob/main/src/lino.lib.mjs

Make a tool, that is able to read and write .lenv files.

Simpliest possible example of the Links Notation ENV file:

```
GITHUB_TOKEN: gh_....
TELEGRAM_TOKEN: 054....
```

So instead of usual `=` we use `: `.

The API should allow to get any env by its reference (name, like GITHUB_TOKEN) (actually last instance of reference/link, because duplicates of references are allowed).

And also to set all instances of reference to a new value.

At the moment we should focus on single links, so the links with only one reference (we will treat it as value).

items.title: Implement LinoEnv library for .lenv files
items.body:
## Summary

This PR implements a proof of concept for a LinoEnv library that can read and write `.lenv` files using the Links Notation format.

### Key Features

- **Custom separator**: Uses `: ` instead of `=` for key-value pairs
- **Duplicate keys support**: Allows multiple instances of the same key
- **Comprehensive API**:
  - `get(reference)` - Gets the last instance of a key
  - `getAll(reference)` - Gets all instances of a key
  - `set(reference, value)` - Sets all instances to a new value
  - `add(reference, value)` - Adds a new instance (allows duplicates)
  - `delete(reference)` - Removes all instances
  - `has(reference)` - Checks if key exists
  - `keys()` - Lists all keys
  - `toObject()` - Converts to plain object
- **Convenience functions**: `readLinoEnv()` and `writeLinoEnv()`

### File Format Example

```
GITHUB_TOKEN: gh_....
TELEGRAM_TOKEN: 054....
```

### Implementation Details

- Written in ES modules (`.mjs`)
- Full test coverage with 22 passing tests
- Includes example usage scripts in `examples/` directory
- Supports empty values, values with spaces, and values with colons
- Handles duplicates correctly (returns last instance via `get()`)

### Test Results


### Files Added
